title: Orchestration frameworks, and a graph that uses the middleware

concept.heading: A framework adds state, named routes, interrupts and checkpoints to the loop you already wrote
paragraphs: LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK and CrewAI all wrap the same loop from Module 1. What they add is worth having once there are branches: state that is explicit between steps, nodes with names you can see in a trace, conditional edges that route on the state, interrupts for a human, and checkpoints so a run resumes after a restart. LangGraph is used here because you have touched it before and because its interrupt and checkpoint model maps cleanly onto the approval gate.

The agent in this lesson has four nodes. The supervisor asks the model for one word, lookup, draft, approval or done, and routes on it. The lookup node runs a bounded loop with read tools only, every call going through the MCP server you built; the draft node asks for text; approval is the next lesson. The MCP server is the agent's only door to the CRM, so every control from Modules 3 to 6 applies to the agent automatically.

The adapter between the async MCP Client and LangGraph's synchronous nodes is thirty lines you write and can debug. langchain-mcp-adapters exists for this, but it lags the MCP SDK's major versions; owning the adapter is the safer bet for a client install.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: Copilot Studio's generative orchestration with topics, or an n8n AI Agent node with sub-workflows. The supervisor is the orchestrator; the nodes are topics; the MCP server is the connector they all share.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: TypedDict state, an event loop on a thread, LangGraph's StateGraph
pythonBlock.intro: Run one asyncio loop on a daemon thread and let ONE task own the Client for its whole life: anyio's cancel scopes must be entered and exited by the same task, so a serve loop that enters once, answers jobs from a queue, and exits once is the whole bridge.

spec: Run uv sync --extra graph. Implement MCPToolSource (loop thread, one Client for the with-block, tools(), call()).
Implement build_graph with the four nodes and the conditional edges per the stub; the lookup node offers read tools only and refuses writes; an unknown route ends the run.
Run the scripted scenario from the check by hand with a replay provider, then run it --live with a free-tier key and watch the supervisor's choices.
Add one span per node using Module 6's tracer so a trace shows supervisor, lookup, draft in order.
askClaudeFor: A one-hour comparison of LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK and CrewAI: what each adds beyond the raw loop, in a table you can show a client.
A review of your adapter's shutdown: does the loop thread stop and the client disconnect on __exit__, even after an exception?

check.summary: The adapter lists and calls the in-process server's tools synchronously; a scripted scenario routes lookup -> draft -> done with find_donor then get_donation_history; the lookup node never executes a write; an unknown route ends safely with the CRM untouched.
